questions.q: What does the heroine have left in the fridge?
o: Half a jar of sour cream
questions.e: In the video: "Imam stres, dugove i pola pavlake u frižideru" — I have stress, debts and half a jar of sour cream in the fridge.

questions.q: How much cash does the heroine have?
questions.e: In the video: "Imam dvije marke" — I have two marks.

questions.q: What is wrong with the TV?
questions.e: In the video: "Uzmi ako hoćeš, ali daljinski ne radi" — take it if you want, but the remote doesn't work.

questions.q: When is the heroine expecting her salary?
o: At the end of the year
questions.e: In the video: "Ako Bog da, u petak" — God willing, on Friday.

questions.q: What does the heroine ask the robber to do at the end?
questions.e: In the video: "Kad već izlaziš, možeš li iznijeti smeće?" — since you're leaving anyway, can you take out the trash?

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.about: Words from the video and their translations

questions.e: Pljačka — a robbery; pljačkati — to rob.
Imati ("to have") requires the accusative case: the plural of dug is dugovi, in the accusative dugove.
Marka is feminine, hence "two": dvije (in Ekavian dve).
After da a personal form is used: ja → kradem.

questions.q: Brate, već si mi ušao u ___.
questions.e: U in answer to "where to?" — accusative case. For inanimate masculine nouns it coincides with the nominative: stan.
